message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Properties**

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Atomic Data** | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | H‑1 (protium), H‑2 (deuterium), H‑3 (tritium) |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | Ionization energy | 13.598 eV (first) |
| | Electron affinity | –0.754 eV |
| | Atomic radius | ~31 pm (covalent) |
| | Van der Waals radius | ~120 pm |
| **Physical State (298 K, 1 atm)** | State | Gas |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C (−423.17 °F) |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C (−434.69 °F) |
| | Density | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ |
| | Molar volume | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Specific heat (Cp) | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Heat of vaporization | 0.449 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Speed of sound | ~1270 m s⁻¹ (in H₂) |
| | Refractive index | 1.000132 (at 589 nm) |
| | Viscosity | 8.76 × 10⁻⁶ Pa s |
| | Thermal conductivity | 0.180 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| **Chemical Properties** | Oxidation states | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride), 0 (H₂) |
| | Bonding | Forms covalent bonds; H₂ is a diatomic molecule with a single σ bond |
| | Reactivity | Highly reactive; forms hydrides with metals, acids with nonmetals |
| | Acid–base behavior | Acts as a weak acid (H⁺ donor) in aqueous solution; forms hydronium (H₃O⁺) |
| | Combustion | Combines with O₂ → H₂O; highly exothermic (ΔH ≈ –286 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Redox potential | Standard electrode potential for H⁺/H₂: 0 V (by definition) |
| | Solubility in water | ~0.0006 g L⁻¹ at 25 °C (very low) |
| | Solubility in organic solvents | Good in nonpolar solvents (e.g., hexane, benzene) |
| | Spectroscopic features | 1s→2p transition at 121.6 nm (Lyman‑α); rotational/vibrational spectra in IR and microwave |
| **Isotopic Variants** | Protium (¹H) | Stable, most abundant |
| | Deuterium (²H) | Stable, 0.015% natural abundance |
| | Tritium (³H) | Radioactive (half‑life 12.32 y), used in nuclear fusion and radiolabeling |
| **Astrophysical & Industrial Relevance** | Stellar fusion | Proton–proton chain, deuterium burning, tritium in fusion reactors |
| | Energy carrier | Hydrogen fuel cells, rocket propellant (LH₂) |
| | Environmental impact | Clean combustion (water vapor); storage challenges (low density, high diffusivity) |
| | Safety | Extremely flammable; forms explosive mixtures with air (1–4 % H₂ in air) |
| | Storage | Cryogenic liquid, high‑pressure gas, metal hydrides, chemical carriers (e.g., ammonia, formic acid) |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Atomic simplicity**: Hydrogen is the lightest element, with only one proton and one electron.
- **Highly reactive**: It readily forms bonds, especially with electronegative elements, and is a key player in both acid–base chemistry and combustion.
- **Energy relevance**: As a clean fuel, hydrogen is central to fuel‑cell technology and future fusion research.
- **Safety considerations**: Its low density and high flammability require careful handling and specialized storage solutions.

Feel free to ask for deeper dives into any specific property or application!
